hierarchy.summary: Cloud Connector Adjustment based on Extreme IT outage

content.text: Extreme IT had an outage that was possible because the ZTP+ connector (which is used regularly for  license checks) was re-activated and the configuration elements were pushed through ZTP+. While this is not a problem if there is only a single active Site Engine, but in the IT case, there was a test site engine that took over from the production one and pushed an empty configuration to the switches in question.
To avoid any erase of configuration the following changes should be done to the ZTP+ connector:

1. When ZTP+ Replies back with Gone (Response.Status.GONE) then future iterations of the cloud connector should ignore any response for image upgrades and configuration changes with the exception of license updating and sitemanager account creation/pw setting.
The cloud connectors still need to go through the first 3 states CONNECT, IMAGE, and CONFIG, it just needs to be selective in what is enforced post Gone received.

If ztp+ onboarding wants to be initiated again, it will require the switch to unconfigure switch all (or you could provide a cli command if it really is needed to keep some of the config like ip during onboarding but I think requiring unconfig switch is better).
1. Similarly, if a configuration was saved on a device manually, then the ZTP+ connector shall be put in the same state as above and not accept/apply any new configuration changes.

hierarchy.summary: FA ZTC - Option to bypass netlogin authentication

content.text: FA ZTC must have a configurable option to bypass netlogin authentication.
A new CLI command will be added in FA to bypass netlogin authentication for a specific client type.
When a netlogin client of the configured type tries to login, the system will automatically authenticate that client.

If netlogin sees the client before FA informs about the configuration, netlogin will follow its regular authentication process. If the client is not authenticated by the regular authentication steps, netlogin will retain the client's information for some time. When it receives the auth bypass related information from FA, it will mark the client as authenticated.

content.text: Recent mandates from the European Union (and alignment with NIST standards) require network infrastructure to transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). Quantum computers pose a significant threat to classical public-key cryptography algorithms (like RSA and ECC) currently used to secure network management and control planes
To achieve PQC compliance, this feature introduces support for the newly standardized NIST post-quantum algorithms into the switch's cryptographic modules

This feature updates both the OpenSSH Server (sshd) and OpenSSH Client modules within Switch Engine (EXOS) to support NIST-approved post-quantum and hybrid cryptographic algorithms. Due to the transitional nature of early PQC adoption, the implementation will heavily rely on hybrid key-exchange mechanisms. This structural pairing ensures that a connection is bound by both a classical algorithm (like X25519) and a post-quantum algorithm (like ML-KEM) simultaneously. If a vulnerability is discovered in the post-quantum algorithm, the session remains secured by the underlying classical mathematical framework.

hierarchy.summary: Implement comprehensive IPv6 First-Hop Security (RA Guard, DHCPv6 Snooping, NDI, Source Guard) for edge protection.

content.text: Currently, Switch Engine (EXOS) robustly supports IPv4 First-Hop Security (FHS) features (such as DHCP Snooping, ARP Validation, and IP Source Guard) as well as IPv6 MLD Snooping for multicast management. However, it lacks a native, comprehensive IPv6 FHS suite. Without these features, IPv6 networks are vulnerable to rogue router advertisements, address spoofing, and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.

This epic details the implementation of the missing IPv6 FHS features. To ensure proper dependencies (as data-plane protections rely on control-plane binding tables), the features will be implemented in the following prioritized order:
Drops unauthorized Router Advertisements (RAs) and Redirect messages to prevent rogue devices from becoming default gateways.
Inspects DHCPv6 messages to block rogue DHCPv6 servers and builds a dynamic IPv6 Binding Database mapping MAC addresses, IPv6 addresses, VLANs, and ports.

Also known as ND Snooping. Validates Neighbor Solicitation (NS) and Neighbor Advertisement (NA) messages against the IPv6 Binding Database to prevent MAC/IP spoofing (the IPv6 equivalent of ARP Validation).
Uses the IPv6 Binding Database to install hardware filters (ACLs/TCAM entries) that drop data-plane traffic from unauthorized IPv6 addresses on untrusted ports.

Due to the 128-bit length of IPv6 addresses, scaling will be lower than IPv4 Source Guard. Platforms with smaller TCAMs (like the 5320) may have strict limits on the number of concurrent IPv6 Source Guard bindings.

, the switch can process these routes at the hardware routing layer, ensuring that routing decisions are made correctly regardless of user ACL configurations.

content.text: Recent mandates from the European Union (and alignment with NIST standards) require network infrastructure to transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). Quantum computers pose a significant threat to classical public-key cryptography algorithms (like RSA and ECC) currently used to secure network management and control planes

If a vulnerability is discovered in the post-quantum algorithm, the session remains secured by the underlying classical mathematical framework.

Due to the 128-bit length of IPv6 addresses, scaling will be lower than IPv4 Source Guard. Platforms with smaller TCAMs (like the 5320) may have strict limits on the number of concurrent IPv6 Source Guard bindings.

content.text: Some systems might experience the Year 2038 problem, also known as Y2038 or the Epochalypse. See explanation below:
┬áMany systems track time as the number of seconds that have passed since January 1, 1970, at 00:00:00 UTC.
┬áOn older systems, this number is stored in a signed 32-bit integer. This data type has a maximum positive value that can only hold 2,147,483,647 seconds after the epoch.

┬áAt 03:14:08 UTC on January 19, 2038, the next second will cause the value to exceed the limit. The number will wrap around to a negative value, which the system will interpret as a time many decades in the past (December 13, 1901)
All systems in EXOS that use the inbuilt time variable need to be updated to use 64-bit integer value instead of the current 32-bit value to avoid the overflow in 2038.

issues.summary: Add Fabric Attach VSA support for non-Extreme Fabric Attach clients on our switch when FA message Authentication is enabled

content.text: Our switch with FA Message authentication enabled on all access ports.
NAC is used on all access ports.
A non-Extreme FA client is connected to an access port and reports itself as, say IpCamera.
Non-Extreme FA client however does not have the default secret FA message authentication key that all Extreme FA devices have.
As a resut, the switch does not include FA-Client-Type VSA (182) in the RADIUS request sent to the RADIUS server.
This defeats the simplicity of FA with NAC for non-Extreme FA Clients.
The FA-Client-Type (182) inbound VSA should always be included, whether the client does FA message authentication or not, and even if it has the wrong key.

And the FA-Client-PSK (183) inbound VSA should also be sent so that the RADIUS server can tell what the FA authentication status of the device is, and the authentication rules can leverage that information.
To recitify this situation on EXOS the following change is required:
1. ┬á ┬áEXOS, with FA message auth enabled, ┬áinclude FA-Client-Type (182) inbound VSA for FA clients not using FA message auth (or having the wrong key)

issues.summary: Cloud Connector Adjustment based on Extreme IT outage

content.text: Extreme IT had an outage that was possible because the ZTP+ connector (which is used regularly for  license checks) was re-activated and the configuration elements were pushed through ZTP+. While this is not a problem if there is only a single active Site Engine, but in the IT case, there was a test site engine that took over from the production one and pushed an empty configuration to the switches in question.
To avoid any erase of configuration the following changes should be done to the ZTP+ connector:

When ZTP+ Replies back with Gone (Response.Status.GONE) then future iterations of the cloud connector should ignore any response for image upgrades and configuration changes with the exception of license updating and sitemanager account creation/pw setting.
The cloud connectors still need to go through the first 3 states CONNECT, IMAGE, and CONFIG, it just needs to be selective in what is enforced post Gone received.

If ztp+ onboarding wants to be initiated again, it will require the switch to unconfigure switch all (or you could provide a cli command if it really is needed to keep some of the config like ip during onboarding but I think requiring unconfig switch is better).
Similarly, if a configuration was saved on a device manually, then the ZTP+ connector shall be put in the same state as above and not accept/apply any new configuration changes.

issues.summary: Add Fabric Attach VSA support for non-Extreme Fabric Attach clients on our switch when FA message Authentication is enabled

content.text: Our switch with FA Message authentication enabled on all access ports.
NAC is used on all access ports.
A non-Extreme FA client is connected to an access port and reports itself as, say IpCamera.
Non-Extreme FA client however does not have the default secret FA message authentication key that all Extreme FA devices have.
As a resut, the switch does not include FA-Client-Type VSA (182) in the RADIUS request sent to the RADIUS server.
This defeats the simplicity of FA with NAC for non-Extreme FA Clients.
The FA-Client-Type (182) inbound VSA should always be included, whether the client does FA message authentication or not, and even if it has the wrong key.

And the FA-Client-PSK (183) inbound VSA should also be sent so that the RADIUS server can tell what the FA authentication status of the device is, and the authentication rules can leverage that information.
To recitify this situation on EXOS the following change is required:
1. ┬á ┬áEXOS, with FA message auth enabled, ┬áinclude FA-Client-Type (182) inbound VSA for FA clients not using FA message auth (or having the wrong key)
